title: Common Migration Misconceptions
content: Misconception 1: The migration happens once a year. Reality: The migration is continuous. Animals are always moving. What changes is location. Misconception 2: River crossings can be scheduled. Reality: Crossings depend on herd behavior and conditions. Guides estimate probability, not timing. Misconception 3: August is the only time to see the migration. Reality: The migration is visible year-round in the Serengeti. August is when it is in the Mara and crossing rivers. Misconception 4: Calving is a minor event. Reality: Calving involves 8,000+ births per day at peak. Predator action is more reliable than crossings. Misconception 5: Any Serengeti safari sees the migration. Reality: The Serengeti is 14,750 square kilometers. You must be positioned in the correct region.
